subject: Re: Direction of factor loadings switches when applied bi-factor model

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Direction of factor loadings switches when applied bi-factor model
parts:
I would say not. 

It's a completely atheoretical way to add constraints, and it will make your model fit worse (and hence all your other parameter estimates less trustworhy).

J

On Wed, 30 May 2018 at 12:11 Monica <finn.hac...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello.  I am trying to apply bi-factor model to a 3 factor model (each factor has 4 indicators).

When I apply bi-factor model, two of indicators on a single factor show negative factor loadings, although they were originally positive.  I am wondering if it is acceptable to constrain factor loadings of these indicators to positive (e.g., 0.1)?

My bi-factor model is:

library(lavaan)

ABC.model <- 'A =~ A1 + A2 + A3 + A4

B =~ B1 + B2 + B3 + B4

C =~ C1 + C2 + C3 + C4

G =~ A1 + A2 + A3 + A4 + B1 + B2 + B3 + B4 + C1 + C2 + C3 + C4'

 fit <- cfa(ABC.model, data=Data, estimator="WLSMV", orthogonal=TRUE)
